=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:lines 285-291 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: In scheduled mode, the no-target log message references `${PR_HEAD_REF}`, which is empty because `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` is null for schedule events.
  WHY: The workflow exits successfully, but operators see a misleading `head ref ''` message; severity was reported as NIT by deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, and z-ai_glm-5_2, and MAJOR by google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite.
- .github/workflows/internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml:lines 6-14 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The unconditional `schedule: cron: "*/5 * * * *"` trigger and scheduled-path permissions run cleanup in every consumer repository without a consumer-side kill switch or opt-in.
  WHY: Consumers can incur unnecessary API usage, log churn, or repeated warnings and failures when `GH_PAT` is absent or scheduled cleanup is not needed; severity was reported as NIT by minimax_minimax-m3 and MAJOR by google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and qwen_qwen3_7-plus.
- workflow-templates/ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml:lines 6-7 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new unconditional `schedule: cron: "*/5 * * * *"` trigger runs in every consumer repository that syncs this wrapper without a dedicated scheduled-path kill switch.
  WHY: Consumers may generate repeated warnings, unnecessary API calls, and workflow activity even when scheduled cleanup is not configured or needed.
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:lines 221-228, 244-249 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Scheduled-mode PR-number extraction emits no entries when active workflow runs lack `pull_requests` linkage, and the downstream empty result provides no diagnostic distinction between no active runs and an API response missing linkage.
  WHY: The fail-open behavior preserves affected runs correctly, but operators cannot determine whether no work existed or PR linkage was omitted.
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:lines 207-213, 246-249 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_cpr_fetch_pr_state_batches` requests `headRefName` and `baseRefName`, but the downstream consumer only checks `$live_pr.state`.
  WHY: Every scheduled batch fetches and stores unused fields, wasting response bytes on the new five-minute hot path.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

- requirement: "Change both close wrappers to pull_request_target with types: [closed]. Keep execution restricted to trusted default-branch workflow code and never check out the PR head. ... Because GitHub will enforce a default public-repository policy blocking pull_request_target on November 2, 2026, explicitly allow this trusted cleanup workflow or provide an existing-scheduler fallback."
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml (event branch that handles github.event.pull_request.head.ref)
  confidence=2

  EVIDENCE: The schedule path runs in addition to the `pull_request.closed` path without a guard ensuring the schedule trigger only runs on the default branch; the linked issue also requires end-to-end coverage of the workflow-list API-error path, but the new tests verify structural changes only.
- requirement: "capture pre-close mergeable and mergeable_state in Phase 7"
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml Phase 7 step
  confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The mergeability fields are fetched and echoed as diagnostics, but are not written to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` as named step outputs for downstream consumption.

  PROBLEM: The log message references `${PR_HEAD_REF}` which evaluates to an empty string because `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` is null in scheduled mode.
  WHY: No runtime failure occurs, but the diagnostic is confusing and should distinguish scheduled and PR-triggered runs.

  WHY: The trigger lacks a consumer-side kill switch and can cause increased API usage, log churn, and warnings when the required PAT is not configured.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:lines 285-291 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When EVENT_NAME=schedule and no target runs are found, the log message "No matching queued/in-progress pull_request workflow runs found for head ref ''" interpolates ${PR_HEAD_REF}, which is empty in scheduled mode because github.event.pull_request.head.ref is null.
  WHY: The workflow exits 0, but operators cannot distinguish the scheduled-mode "no active runs found" path from a bug.
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:lines 221-228 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Scheduled-mode PR-number extraction jq-r '.workflow_runs[] | (.pull_requests // [])[].number | select(type == "number")' emits zero entries when active pull_request workflow runs lack the pull_requests linkage array.
  WHY: Affected runs are preserved correctly, but an empty pr-numbers.txt and subsequent no-target branch provide no way to distinguish no active runs from an API response that omitted pull_requests linkage.
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr-close.yml:lines 207-213 (GraphQL selection set) vs lines 246-249 (consumer) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_cpr_fetch_pr_state_batches` requests headRefName and baseRefName in the GraphQL query but the only downstream consumer checks $live_pr.state.
  WHY: The two extra fields are fetched on every PR in every batch and stored in the merged output file but never read.
- .github/workflows/internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml:lines 6-8 (new schedule trigger), lines 12-14 (new pull-requests: read permission) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A new `schedule: cron: "*/5 * * * *"` trigger and `pull-requests: read` permission are added without a consumer opt-in repo-var or workflow-level kill switch.
  WHY: Consumers can incur approximately 288 runs/day, API spend, and recurrent warnings or checkout failures when `GH_PAT` is missing.
- Requirement: "Change both close wrappers to pull_request_target with types: [closed]. Keep execution restricted to trusted default-branch workflow code and never check out the PR head. ... Because GitHub will enforce a default public-repository policy blocking pull_request_target on November 2, 2026, explicitly allow this trusted cleanup workflow or provide an existing-scheduler fallback." (from linked issue Suggested fix; the implementer chose the existing-scheduler fallback path.)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml (event branch that handles github.event.pull_request.head.ref)
  Evidence of absence: The schedule path runs in addition to the pull_request.closed path. The PR adds the schedule but does not add a guard that ensures the schedule trigger only runs on the default branch. More critically, the linked issue's "stop suppressing workflow-list API errors so future failures distinguish trigger suppression from lookup failure" is implemented (the || echo fallbacks are removed), but there is no test that exercises the API-error path end-to-end.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- Requirement: CLAUDE.md §20.D changelog fragment structure (lead paragraph of 3-5 sentences, "The numbers that matter" table when measurable, audience closing paragraph, optional "For contributors" subsection).
  Expected change site: changelog.d/4258-conflict-safe-pr-close.md
  Evidence of absence: The fragment is two lines: a one-line section marker and a one-sentence headline with optional second sentence. There is no blank-line-separated lead paragraph, no numbers table, no "What this means for <audience>" closing paragraph, and no "For contributors" subsection. §20.D is the contractual fragment format and §20.A applies to this PR.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
